clue.text: Electrician originally serving private estates

definitions.note: Sparks is the traditional nickname for an electrician

indicators.note: originally asks for the word serving at its origin, its opening letter

parts.note: parks are the grounds of private country estates

explanation.surface: An electrician who started out working on the grounds of big private estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is the long-standing slang nickname for an electrician, from the sparks of the trade.

clue.text: Image promoter given right to publish abroad

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, who promotes an image
a claim is a right to something

explanation.surface: A publicist given the rights to publish overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, spreading news far and wide.

clue.text: Disproved what nanny might have done? Again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a nanny goat may butt with her head

explanation.surface: A childminder's actions questioned and repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The nanny is not a childminder but a female goat, which butts.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute or disprove it.

clue.text: A shrimp, maybe, but inconsiderate to drunkards?

indicators.note: to drunkards means as slurred by tipsy speakers

parts.note: an inconsiderate person is selfish

explanation.surface: A small creature or person who is thoughtless towards heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs the S of SELFISH into SH, giving SHELLFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is one example of a shellfish, a crustacean.

clue.text: Half-hearted physician married in 1946, perhaps

parts.note: St Luke is called the beloved physician in the New Testament
a year standing for a period of conflict; the scanned year should be a war year such as 1940

explanation.surface: A doctor who wed just after the war and is lacking in enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: As held the year reads 1946, after the Second World War ended; the wordplay needs a wartime year, so a digit has been misread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, literally tepid, is used figuratively for lacking enthusiasm or commitment.

clue.text: He painted La Gioconda, driven mad after loss of capital

indicators.note: mad suggests letters crazily rearranged
the capital letter of Gioconda, its opening G, is lost

explanation.surface: The Mona Lisa, maddened after leaving the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss of capital' drops G from GIOCONDA, and 'mad' rearranges LA IOCONDA DRIVEN. La Gioconda is the Italian name of the Mona Lisa, which this painter made.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance artist who painted the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Competitive rider always securing opening

indicators.note: securing means holding the opening inside

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A horse rider in competition who always keeps a gap secure.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider taking part in eventing, a multi-discipline competition.

clue.text: Sound quality associated with type of horse or cow

indicators.note: sound signals a word as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: an air is a quality or manner
a shire is a breed of heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: A quality of tone linked to a breed of horse or cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR, a Scottish town, is heard as AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ayrshire is a Scottish breed of dairy cattle, so an example of a cow.

clue.text: Have doubts about water vapour and what it may produce

parts.note: mist is water vapour suspended in the air
damp air can corrode iron into rust

explanation.surface: Questioning whether damp air really causes corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to be suspicious of, so to have doubts about.

clue.text: In Mexico it may be felt on one's head

definitions.text: In Mexico it may be felt on one's head

parts.words: In Mexico it may be felt on one's head
parts.note: felt reads as a sensation, but it is the fabric of a broad-brimmed Mexican hat

explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat, often made of felt or straw, worn on the head.

clue.text: Girls coming out to go over state ruins

indicators.note: the debutantes are placed over and around the state abbreviation

parts.note: debs are debutantes, girls making their coming-out into society
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Debutantes leaving to travel around a nation in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something destroyed, so ruins in the sense of wreckage.

clue.text: Charge a great deal, entering a number of vessels

indicators.note: the great-deal word goes inside the word for charge

parts.note: to charge a glass is to fill it
a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: Someone charging a hefty sum to join a group of boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet, a group of ships or boats sailing together.

clue.text: One may make a deep impression in the studio

definitions.text: One may make a deep impression in the studio

parts.words: One may make a deep impression in the studio
parts.note: sounds like a memorable artist, but literally describes someone cutting lines into a metal plate

explanation.definitionFit: An artist who cuts designs into plates with acid or a needle literally makes deep impressions.

clue.text: Malefactor pinching ring is furiously reviled

indicators.note: the jumbled letters grip the ring between them
furiously suggests letters thrown about wildly

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer who stole a ring is angrily condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges REVILED into EVILDER, and 'pinching' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is one who does wrong, a synonym for a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Gang-girl that's in hospital ' department soothing agent

indicators.note: the gangster's girl and that's sit inside the department

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department
a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend in a hospital ward is given something calming.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a substance that softens and soothes the skin.

clue.text: Surrounded by a thousand and one diamonds

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone encircled by a vast hoard of gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, so surrounded by.

clue.text: Tree-dwelling fellow, a right Point drag at first

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Tree-dwelling fellow, a right Point drag at first', is garbled: A R BORE A L cannot be matched to 'fellow', 'Point' and 'at first'
annotationWithheld.clue: Tree-dwelling fellow, a right Point drag at first

clue.text: It restricts woman in navy, causing annoyance

indicators.note: it closes around the rest as a boundary

parts.note: it is taken as written

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the navy abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Something confines a woman serving in the fleet, which is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritant as an adjective means causing irritation, so causing annoyance.

clue.text: Posted speaker's bouquet

indicators.note: a speaker's version is the word as it is heard

parts.note: bouquet is the scent of a wine

explanation.surface: A bouquet of flowers mailed to someone who gives speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent is the past tense of send, which in mail terms means posted.

clue.text: Way the French carry equipment for game

indicators.note: the way word holds the equipment inside it

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
kit is equipment
les is French for the plural the

explanation.surface: The way the French carry gear for their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a pub game of knocking down pins with a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles is a bowling game in which pins are knocked over.

clue.text: A small number glorify English peers

parts.note: No is the abbreviation, the shortened form, of number
to bless God is to glorify him

explanation.surface: A few people praise the English aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblesse is the nobility, the class of peers.

clue.text: Tropical fruit a theologian kept in jar

indicators.note: the article and the theologian are held inside the jolt word

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: Exotic fruit that a divinity scholar preserved in a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is the pomelo, a large citrus fruit of tropical Asia.

clue.text: Directions in duty lists upset legislator

indicators.note: the directions are placed inside the upset lists
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: rotas are lists of duties
E and N are compass directions

explanation.surface: Instructions on shift rosters annoy a lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads the duty lists bottom to top; 'Directions' are two compass points side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a legislative body.

clue.text: It's nothing in France, having books about the East

indicators.note: the books abbreviation goes around the French word

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A traveller with nothing but reading matter about Eastern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the traditional name for the countries of the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: Unusually evil lot, albeit at first apt to change

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appearing in an unusual arrangement
at first takes the opening letter of albeit

explanation.surface: A wicked group who are nonetheless liable to shift their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives A from albeit, and 'Unusually' rearranges EVIL, LOT and that A.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile describes something unstable, liable to change quickly and unpredictably.

clue.text: Back European girl detailed for position in ballet

indicators.note: back tells us the assembled run is read from right to left
de-tailed, the girl's name losing its tail

parts.note: Tracey is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from Europe is assigned a place at the back of the ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the tail Y off TRACEY, and 'Back' turns E plus TRACE (ETRACE) right round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecarte is a ballet position in which the body is angled with a leg extended to the side.

clue.text: To goad sons is uncalled for

parts.note: to needle someone is to goad them
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for sons

explanation.surface: Provoking one's children is unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, so not called for.

clue.text: New rite framed by a lot of old language scholars

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the shortened language as in a frame
a lot of means most of the word, not all of it

parts.note: Latin is the classic old language

indicators.note: new signals the letters made into a new order

explanation.surface: A freshly devised ceremony set in an ancient tongue for academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' means most of the word: only its final letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are learned people, particularly those versed in literature.

clue.text: Person examining canopy over four-poster bed

definitions.meaning: one who tests or tries something out
an old word for a canopy over a bed, especially a four-poster

explanation.definitionFit: One who tests things is an examiner, and the word also names a bed canopy.
